fields.description:
After beating Cataclysm i got really hyped about the cape section and decided that i wanted more so i went further in cape mechanics and built this hack, this hack is the ultimate cape challenge a full pit hack featuring a lot of cape tricks since normal flight till the most deep pit of cape glitches.

This is a challenge made by me for myself, so we have 3 endings, if you don't wanna play the entire hack you can go for an any% run and for those who wanna a real challenge you can go for 100%, this is the first pit hack where you can decide your route, so open lunar magic, see all rooms, route your path and go for the TAS.

14 cape rooms, 3 bosses, some secrets and some extra challenges!

Hope you enjoy it and let's have fun!

Fixes 1.1
- 3 moons had problems so i fixed
- added a big door in room 102 to avoid useless damage boost
- added credits for the first 100% blind clear

fields.description:
Well, after a long time, The Pit Level 3 has been completed.

This hack was started in 2015 and I worked hard on it until mid-2017. For personal reasons, I was forced to interrupt progress and it was practically stopped until 2022. From 2022 onwards I managed to work hard on it again and finish it.

The focus of this hack was not difficulty, although it is somewhat complex. My goal was to make a fun hack. Because it was mostly made between 2015 and 2017, this hack is made up of many shelljumps, yumps, keyjumps and things like that. Nowadays, that's not as cool as it was in 2015, but I didn't have much of a choice. I managed to change many rooms and eliminate some repeated shelljumps, but overall if I were to change everything, I would have to do a new hack.

FULL HACK VIDEO: https://youtu.be/mrlO3VQiz9U

Anyway, that was the most I could do. Although this hack is full of shelljumps/keyjumps, it also has some cool tricks, as you will see in some rooms.

NOTE: The water room (room 112) is different from what appears in the video. I changed it because it was generating a lot of lag, but unfortunately I couldn't change it in the video, as the TAS was desyncing.

NOTE 2: The crash at the end of the video was for pure fun, it is not mandatory. The hack ends as soon as you kill the boss.

That's it, download and enjoy!

fields.description:
You exit from your last-played level victorious. The design was fine, if not familiar, but engaging and fun. You jumped over the pits, you avoided the munchers, and touching the goal tape felt satisfying enough. The gimmicks were really neat, and some of the more unique elements ignited your imagination about the yet unplayed levels that await on the road ahead. What new obstacles would the creator expect you to overcome? As you ponder this, traversing the overworld of the hack you are currently playing, you see a streak of green and yellow flash across the sky. Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it’s a caped union plumber indulging in aerodynamic equestrianism! At first they look ridiculous and awkward. It doesn’t even look fun, but, you can’t stop watching. How are they even doing that? It looks hard, but also kind of interesting. Their horse doesn’t even have wings! Why does it keep sticking its tongue out?! You think to yourself, “Could I do it too?” A disembodied voice whispers back into your thoughts, “You can, if you try.”

Chinese astrology says the Year of the Horse is upon us! This first of its kind Yoshi horse flight hack comes as an unlikely collaboration between 4 joint 2006 Time Magazine ‘Person of the Year’ award recipients. The premise is simple, in every level you must eat the 5 golden berries and then hatch and collect your prize. The path to credits has 9 levels, and there are 4 bonus levels after the credits that include 3 guest levels. This hack is not a tutorial. It is a challenge that tests your understanding and consistency of control, and allows you to improve as you go. There is a simple practice level within the hack that provides a space to work on your horse and horseless flight fundamentals freely.

Good luck, and safe flying. We believe in you.

fields.description: Hello, this is my first hack, and also my first hack to be released on SMW Central. I loved creating this project and finally releasing it. This hack is a Kaizo Grandmaster shell hack. It all came from my evolution in creating previous projects that failed, but I wisely used every trick, every adjustment, every cool thing to include in a hack. I worked hard and achieved a dream. This is no joke, this is a goal achieved and a great step forward in my life and dreams. I hope you enjoy this hack, I dedicated myself a lot to it, good luck!

fields.description:
"Yoshi is a tool to be used and then discarded."

These words have long been held as absolute truth in Kaizo level design. Every appearance of Yoshi is followed by a swift press of the A button. But Yoshi has had enough, in a surprising twist he captures Mario and locks him away. It's not clear what Yoshi is planning, but Mario doesn't intend to find out. He escapes Yoshi's dungeon and sets out on a quest to find 3 elemental powers (switch palaces) to stop Yoshi before it's too late.

Yoshi's Revenge is my second hack, releasing over seven years after my first, the somewhat infamous Salty Sagan World. My main goal was to take the same largely traditional Kaizo gameplay from my first hack and polish it up a lot, keeping the fun and reducing the frustration, as well as adding a little bit of chocolate sprinkles. Additionally, this game is designed with replayability in mind, has intriguing and rewarding secrets (which aren't portraits or an overarching puzzle), and a rich post-game that offers a variety of optional challenges such as: more difficult levels, endurance tests, playing under restrictions and speedrunning, for players who want to test their skills further.

This is also a game with a lot of freedom. There are over 200 paths through the game, so you have the opportunity to prioritize the levels that look most appealing. Out of the 46 total exits, you should only see 26 or 27 on a standard playthrough (assuming you don't go out of your way to play extra levels). To help you make informed decisions, each level has a length and difficulty rating. Secret exits are intentionally made very difficult to find without the hints provided in the game. As you learn how the world is connected, you will have more agency to play through the game however you want on repeat playthroughs. My intention was to make learning the world layout something that could be mastered in itself, similar to how some 2D Metroid games work. There is even a Metroid Zero Mission style gallery that rewards you for finding specific paths through the game and playing well. However, there is only one ending! If you're not interested in secrets or playing more levels than necessary, then rest assured, that is also a perfectly valid way to enjoy this game.

As for the ever-divisive topic of difficulty... to be blunt, I think some people read way too much into difficulty ratings on SMWCental as if it's some kind of objective science, when it could not be further from. Especially for a game as big and open as this one, it's impossible to accurately capture the difficulty with a single rating. Some things in this game could be beaten by almost anyone. Some hidden post-game challenges in this game are approaching the limit of what is humanly possible. This is entirely by design, as I want players with a variety of skill levels to be able to set their own goals within the hack, and maybe even encourage them to improve by offering, but not forcing, a challenge that is just outside their comfort zone. The chosen difficulty of 'Master' is intended to reflect the skill required to somewhat comfortably obtain the save file star shown in screenshot 2. While just beating the game is certainly easier, especially since you have a lot of freedom in choosing what levels you play, I suspect you may still stumble into some uncomfortable difficulty spikes if you don't have a lot of experience with SMW under your belt.

With that said, I'd like to emphasize that I was not really aiming for a specific difficulty while making this game. First and foremost, I wanted to explore a wide range of ideas, both mechanically and aesthetically, and make levels that felt satisfying to blast through, especially once you know them. Generally, I wanted them to put up enough of a fight to unquestionably feel like Kaizo while also having enough leeway to allow for player expression and leave room for improvement on repeat playthroughs. If I succeeded, there should hopefully be a noticeable difference between beating a level and mastering it.

It's very hard to believe it has been over six years since I started working on this game. What started as a simple follow-up to Salty Sagan World, became a massive passion project that I poured my heart and soul into for probably many thousands of hours. Being a Kaizo game, and one that at times features some daring decisions, it will undoubtedly generate some frustration - and releasing it has me very nervous. Actually, I believe panicking is a more apt word. But at the very least, I am incredibly proud of what I have made, and I say this from the bottom of my heart:

If you are a player, I hope you will enjoy playing this game.
If you are a viewer, I hope this game will provide many opportunities for you to say KEKW.
And, if you are a creator, I hope this game will inspire you to make something amazing.

Please see the included text files for information related to save data and things that have been patched.

If you'd like to see the game in action, you can watch the release trailer for it here:
https://youtu.be/fqbJBcCcdOo

The complete soundtrack is now available here (contains spoilers!):
https://youtu.be/A2l3bq0RbyQ

Updated to version 1.1.1 on 18th of May 2026. Unless a major issue is discovered, this will be the final update. The main purpose of this update is to improve the overall player experience, especially for first playthroughs, by (hopefully) making some obstacles a bit more readable, fixing some jank and crashes, adding a bit more guidance for some secrets and changing some existing hints to be more direct. There's also a few quality-of-life additions. Finally, as a way for me to express my gratitude to everyone who's played Yoshi's Revenge, there's a small amount of DLC (brand new content!) that both new and old players can enjoy. Please consult the changelog for all the details. Existing save files are compatible with 1.1.1.

fields.changelog:
1. In Ominous Castle #2, Bowser's hit box should
work on all emulators. But I still couldn't get
the mechakoopas to hit though. :(
2. Changed the NPC Follower Sprite to version 4.5
to show the message indicator, the talk button is
up instead of X/Y, and gave it walking animation
on platform sprites.
3. I changed certain boss battles to not have
Boom Booms/too many chucks, so it doesn't ramp up
the difficulty.
4. Added Multiple Midway Check Points from Kevin's
Rerty Uberasm system, added a second check point
in Ominous Castle #2 in front of the boss door, and
added a key so the player doesn't have to recollect
all the key coins to progress.
5. Changed the Boss fight in Dark Forest to not drop
so many apples at once.
6. Changed the layout of Ominous Castle #2 sub-level,
so that the NPC doesn't jump through the ceiling.

fields.description:
Castlemania - REVAMPED serves primarily as a visual upgrade to the original 2024 Castlemania release. The main focus in this ‘remaster’ is to provide a more appropriate experience for the hardware, as well as improve various design choices. In addition - REVAMPED brings subweapons to the mix, which offers an extra layer to the original’s gameplay.

Good luck, have fun and THANK YOU FOR PLAYING!

- Fixed misplaced P-switch in "Down the machinery"

- Crash's moveset has been expanded! Now along with the Spin he can do the body Slam and slide Attack seen in Crash Bandicoot 2:Cortex Strikes back!
- A new crate type has been added: the gray reforced crate, this crate can only be broken with the body slam
- Several levels have been tweaked to work better and explore the new moves and incorporate the new crate type.
- Golden Wumpas have been added to nearly every level(the exceptions are levels that feature some kind of challenge related to wumpas in the retroachievements site)

- The dificulty curve has been adjusted in several levels to offer a more aproachable and fair dificulty for all players!

- The Upwards Fireballs patch have been added
- 3 songs have been changed to free some space in the rom.
- The title screen now notes that this is an enhanced version of the hack so it can be easily identifiable from the previous version who don't have these new features.

- Added "optimized spotlight" patch to reduce slowdown on spotlight levels

v1.10
- Tweaked the crouch jump so it is easier and faster to use
- Adjusted dificulty and level design through lots of levels in the hack, adjusting them so they are more fun to play.

- Adjusted the checkpoints in "Bye Bye retro world"

fields.description:
Crash Bandicoot and the retro dimension is a Crash Bandicoot themed Super Mario World Romhack! This hack aims to mix the elements of a Crash Bandicoot game into Super Mario World. You will be playing as our favorite Marsupial Crash Bandicoot and the hack have been designed to feel like a proper Crash game in many ways within the SMW mechanics, so lots of changes, tweaks and elements have been implemented to achieve this goal creating a unique experience mixing the best of Crash and SMW together in one package.

With this being said, this hack is pretty much a full-on Crash Bandicoot adventure within Super Mario World featuring 86 levels with 102 exits to find, and also 94 gems&86 relics to collect.

It also features new mechanics such as Crash being able to use his iconic moves, custom graphics, lots of custom music(especially from the Crash Bandicoot franchise), and lots of ASM.

With the update v1.20 the hack has been enhanced and expanded with some new features:

- Crash’s moveset has been expanded with the addition of the Body Slam and Slide seen in Crash Bandicoot 2 Cortex strikes back
- Level design has been tweaked to acomodate the new moves
- The dificulty curve has been adjusted to be more adaptive for all kinds of players
- Golden wumpas have been added, these are worth 10 wumpas and have been placed in risky or hard to reach places as a icentive for exploration.
- Several improvements across the game and more.

Check the trailer for this update here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tiS5Dvvu6N4

The hack also features retroachievements support. https://retroachievements.org/game/34882

fields.description:
This hack is a tribute hack for one of my favorite games of all times: Dragon's Dogma. The story varies a little, because this is not the tale of the arisen, but of the humble plumber Mario, who lost everything in a dragon's attack. Now he seeks for vengeance and goes out into the world, which is called "Gransys".
This hack is a 46-expert-exit hack, with a lot of variety, a semi-open world (there are three ways to get to the any% ending) that contains a lot of secrets and easter-eggs for Dragon's Dogma. Pawns are scattered around the world, waiting for the arisen, but helping Mario with advices.

Prepare yourself for 46 flow-focussed-levels, with some cryptic levels to get your brain into action. Enjoy the variety of all exists, because no level feels the same.



I hope you'll have a great time playing this hack.

Additionally, here is a major gameplay spoiler:
The final boss's max health is reduced by 1, for each wakestone (moon) you collect. So keep your eyes open.

name: Crash Bandicoot and the Retro Dimension 2 - The Crystal Hunt

fields.description:
Crash Bandicoot is back for another adventure on the Super Nintendo!

Crash Bandicoot and the Retro dimension 2: The Crystal Hunt is a Crash Bandicoot themed Super Mario World Romhack and a sequel to Crash Bandicoot and the Retro Dimension. Just like it’s predecessor this hack aims to mix the elements of the classic Crash Bandicoot games into Super Mario World creating a unique experience that mix the best of both worlds.

Crash can use his iconic moves such as the spin, the slide and body slam and lots of new things have been added to make the hack feel more like a proper Crash Bandicoot game. Some of those things includes lots of custom music( with a lot of them being from the Crash Bandicoot series), NPCS characters and bosses from the Crash universe, custom graphics, lots of ASM modyfing some of the mechanics and more

This time around the hack features a more open design where the player can play through the game with more freedom for exploring the map in wathever order the player feels like. The hack features 93 levels with 120 crystals and 93 gems and relics to collect. It’s a bigger adventure than the last one.

Story: One month after the last adventure Dr.Cortex found out a new source of power in the retro dimension, power crystals! He intends to use the crystals on his new evil plan to power his Doomsday machine a device capable of distorting reality itself. Now it’s up to Crash Bandicoot and his friends to save the day! The player must collect power crystals at the end of each level to progress through the game and defeat the evil Dr. Neo Cortex.

The hack is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

fields.description:
Welcome to Aperitif! A beginner hack to hopefully whet your appetite for your full Kaizo meal! There are 13 exits and each level adds on to the one before it. While not a full tutorial hack Aperitif starts with simple jumps and adds mechanics as you go! There are also some additional challenges for players who already have some Kaizo completions. Each level has a Padlock Coin™ you can lock in and try to collect! In addition there is a hard mode that strings the normal mode levels together into one SUPER LEVEL!

I hope you enjoy playing Aperitif, and if this is one of your first Kaizo hacks I hope it leads to you playing more SMW hacks and joining the wonderful SMW community!

Note: While there is no additional exit for getting all the Padlock Coins™ it does unlock an additional level for you to play!
Another note: Beating Hard Mode does give you an exit it is the same exit as the final level of normal mode and does not go beyond the normal 13 exits.
One final note: In order to make sure a beginner could play this I had my teenage son with 0 SMW experience play the hack as the first playtester. GG to THE BOI™

raw_fields.description:
Welcome to Aperitif! A beginner hack to hopefully whet your appetite for your full Kaizo meal! There are 13 exits and each level adds on to the one before it. While not a full tutorial hack Aperitif starts with simple jumps and adds mechanics as you go! There are also some additional challenges for players who already have some Kaizo completions. Each level has a Padlock Coin™ you can lock in and try to collect! In addition there is a hard mode that strings the normal mode levels together into one SUPER LEVEL!

I hope you enjoy playing Aperitif, and if this is one of your first Kaizo hacks I hope it leads to you playing more SMW hacks and joining the wonderful SMW community!

Note: While there is no additional exit for getting all the Padlock Coins™ it does unlock an additional level for you to play!
Another note: Beating Hard Mode does give you an exit it is the same exit as the final level of normal mode and does not go beyond the normal 13 exits.
One final note: In order to make sure a beginner could play this I had my teenage son with 0 SMW experience play the hack as the first playtester. GG to THE BOI™
